units.source_text: 右方的人便称赞起自己的《空穗物语》画卷来：

en.t: The people on the right began praising their own illustrated scroll of The Tale of Utsuho:

units.source_text: “俊荫远游中国，途遇风波，飘泊到人地生疏的波斯国。

en.t: “Toshikage traveled far to China, met storms along the way, and drifted to the unfamiliar land of Persia.

units.source_text: 然而不屈不挠，定要成遂初志。

en.t: Yet he remained unyielding and was determined to fulfill his original ambition.

units.source_text: 终于学得了旷世无比的弹琴妙技，名闻于外国朝廷及日本国内，又传之于后世。

en.t: At last he mastered an unmatched art of playing the koto, became famous at foreign courts and within Japan, and passed his skill down to later generations.
He may truly be called a man of vast talent!

units.source_text: 这画的笔法也兼备中国、日本两国风格，趣味之丰富，无可比拟了。”

en.t: The brushwork of these paintings also combines the styles of both China and Japan, and the richness of their charm is beyond compare.”

units.source_text: 这画卷用白色纸，裱纸是青色的，轴用黄玉。

en.t: The scroll was made with white paper, mounted with blue backing paper, and fitted with a yellow jade roller.

units.source_text: 画是当代名人飞鸟部常则所绘，字是大书法家小野道风所书。

en.t: The pictures were painted by the celebrated artist of the day, Asukabe no Tsunenori, and the calligraphy was written by the great calligrapher Ono no Michikaze.

units.source_text: 全体新颖多趣，光彩耀目。

en.t: The whole work was fresh, full of interest, and dazzling in its brilliance.

units.source_text: 左方无法反驳，于是右方得胜了。

en.t: The left side had no way to refute them, and so the right side won.
